A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the HCTs are potent ribonucleotide diphosphate reductase inhibitors, that they inhibit the incorporation of [methyl-3H]thiamine into DNA, and that they inhibit DNA synthesis without affecting RNA synthesis.
3-AP has the most potential for clinical development.
3-AP was the most active compound of the series tested. 3-AMP was the second most active compound of this series tested. 5-AP was the least active compound of this study.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HCTs can be considered to be a new class of ribonucleotde reductase inhibitors that are distinct from the clinically used inhibitors hydroxyurea and cisplatin.
the HCTs can be modified to increase their activity against ribonucleotide reduction and, thus, against cancer cells.
3-AP is the most promising HCT in the treatment of human cancers.
